Capacity and power are separate A 10 kWh battery with 5 kW output may theoretically supply a steady 1 kW load for less than 10 hours after reserve and losses, but it cannot necessarily start or run every appliance. A battery with high output but small capacity can run larger loads briefly but empties quickly.

chunks.sourceTitle: Power You Control: Australian Home Energy Systems Guide
chunks.text: Capacity and power are separate A 10 kWh battery with 5 kW output may theoretically supply a steady 1 kW load for less than 10 hours after reserve and losses, but it cannot necessarily start or run every appliance. A battery with high output but small capacity can run larger loads briefly but empties quickly. Simple backup runtime estimate Runtime hours = usable battery energy multiplied by assumed discharge efficiency, divided by average essential-load power. Use average power for runtime and peak or starting power for equipment compatibility. Refrigerators, pumps and compressors can have starting demands above their running power. Battery sizing workflow 1 Define the job. Savings, backup, demand control, grid services or off-grid. 2 Use interval data. Separate solar exports, post-sunset imports, peak-period use and overnight baseload. 3 Set the daily energy target.

chunks.sourceTitle: Power You Control: Australian Home Energy Systems Guide
chunks.text: Separate solar exports, post-sunset imports, peak-period use and overnight baseload. 3 Set the daily energy target. Avoid sizing from household size or solar kW alone. 4 Set the power target. List appliances that may run together and their starting loads. 5 Reserve energy. Decide how much must remain for outages or battery protection. 6 Model solar recharge. Check winter and cloudy conditions, not only annual surplus. 7 Include losses and degradation. Use conservative values from warranted performance. 8 Test multiple capacities. Compare marginal savings and unmet goals. 9 Check physical and electrical fit. Placement, switchboard, inverter, network and approvals. 10 Document control settings. Tariff, reserve, schedules, export and program participation.

chunks.text: POWER YOU CONTROL AUSTRALIAN HOME ENERGY SYSTEMS GUIDE Snapshot: 25 August 2026 39 For solar self-consumption Start with typical daily solar exports and electricity imports from late afternoon to morning. A battery much larger than regular available surplus may charge from the grid or remain partly empty. A battery much larger than overnight load may carry unused capacity into the next solar day. For backup Build an essential-load table: Load Running W Starting W if relevant Hours needed Daily Wh Refrigeration Lighting Communications Medical or accessibility equipment Water or wastewater pump Selected heating or cooling Other essential load Keep high-energy discretionary loads off the backup board unless the design deliberately supports them. Battery chemistry and construction Many current home batteries use lithium-ion cells.

chunks.sourceTitle: Power You Control: Australian Home Energy Systems Guide
chunks.text: For backup Build an essential-load table: Load Running W Starting W if relevant Hours needed Daily Wh Refrigeration Lighting Communications Medical or accessibility equipment Water or wastewater pump Selected heating or cooling Other essential load Keep high-energy discretionary loads off the backup board unless the design deliberately supports them. Battery chemistry and construction Many current home batteries use lithium-ion cells. Common families include lithium iron phosphate and nickel-manganese-cobalt chemistries. They differ in energy density, thermal behaviour, voltage, supply chain and cell design. Good safety depends on the complete tested system, battery management, enclosure, installation and operation, not chemistry label alone. Lead-acid batteries remain in some off-grid or legacy systems.

chunks.sourceTitle: Power You Control: Australian Home Energy Systems Guide
chunks.text: Good safety depends on the complete tested system, battery management, enclosure, installation and operation, not chemistry label alone. Lead-acid batteries remain in some off-grid or legacy systems. They are heavy, have ventilation and maintenance considerations, and generally tolerate less usable depth of discharge than modern lithium systems. Flow and sodium-ion technologies may appear in some applications, but availability and approval must be checked at purchase time. Never mix modules, chemistries, ages or firmware unless the approved design and manufacturer instructions explicitly permit it. AC-coupled and DC-coupled batteries DC coupling Solar and battery share a hybrid inverter or DC pathway. Potential strengths: 1 Fewer conversion stages when charging directly from solar. 1 Integrated control in a new system.

chunks.sourceTitle: Power You Control: Australian Home Energy Systems Guide
chunks.text: Potential strengths: 1 Fewer conversion stages when charging directly from solar. 1 Integrated control in a new system. 1 Possible ability to use solar DC above inverter AC output to charge the battery, subject to design. Questions: 1 Battery compatibility and future lock-in. 1 What happens if the hybrid inverter fails. 1 Backup and black-start behaviour. 1 Array voltage and charge-power limits.

chunks.text: POWER YOU CONTROL AUSTRALIAN HOME ENERGY SYSTEMS GUIDE Snapshot: 25 August 2026 40 AC coupling The battery has a separate battery inverter on the AC side. Potential strengths: 1 Flexible retrofit to serviceable existing solar. 1 Solar and battery can sometimes operate more independently. 1 Separate replacement pathways. Questions: 1 Extra conversion losses. 1 Coordination in an outage. 1 Network export and inverter-capacity rules. 1 Space, switchboard and metering requirements. Neither architecture is universally superior. Compare efficiency, compatibility, backup, serviceability, cost and future expansion for the property. Battery with no rooftop solar A grid-charged battery may shift energy, reduce demand charges, provide backup or join a grid-service program. Test: 1 Off-peak to peak price difference after losses. 1 Daily supply and demand charges.

chunks.sourceTitle: Power You Control: Australian Home Energy Systems Guide
chunks.text: Test: 1 Off-peak to peak price difference after losses. 1 Daily supply and demand charges. 1 Ability to charge within the cheap window. 1 Rules about grid charging and program eligibility. 1 Carbon implications of the charging period if relevant to the goal. 1 Whether a thermal store or load shifting solves the problem more cheaply. 1 Whether rooftop or shared solar may be added later. Financial model Use annual cash flows, not a simple claim that capacity multiplied by tariff equals savings. Include: 1 Installed price after clearly identified incentives. 1 Financing and fees. 1 Charging source: forgone solar export or grid purchase. 1 Round-trip and standby losses. 1 Battery control strategy and reserve. 1 Avoided import by time period. 1 Export credits forgone. 1 Demand-charge savings if measured and realistic. 1 Program payments and participation conditions.

chunks.text: POWER YOU CONTROL AUSTRALIAN HOME ENERGY SYSTEMS GUIDE Snapshot: 25 August 2026 41 1 Tariff and household-change scenarios. 1 Residual value or disposal cost only if evidence supports it. Marginal value method Model several usable capacities. The first kWh of storage may cycle frequently and displace expensive imports. Additional capacity may cycle less often and have lower value. The best economic size is often smaller than the size that maximises self-sufficiency. Resilience value Blackout support, medical continuity, refrigeration, water pumping and avoiding business interruption can have real value, but keep that value separate from bill savings so the decision remains honest. Current national battery support Eligible small-scale batteries connected to new or existing solar can create certificates under the national small-scale scheme.

Current rules include capacity, product, installation, accreditation, documentation and virtual-power-plant capability requirements. Certificate factors and capacity tiers change over time. chunks.sourceTitle: Power You Control: Australian Home Energy Systems Guide
chunks.text: POWER YOU CONTROL AUSTRALIAN HOME ENERGY SYSTEMS GUIDE Snapshot: 25 August 2026 43 Blackouts, Backup and Household Resilience Backup must be designed, wired and tested. A battery sitting beside a grid-connected solar system does not automatically keep the home powered. Why ordinary solar usually stops in an outage Grid-connected inverters must stop energising the grid when supply fails, protecting workers and the public. Backup requires an approved system that isolates the home or selected circuits from the grid and controls solar and battery operation as a safe island. Whole-home versus essential-circuit backup Essential circuits Selected loads are moved to a backed-up section of the switchboard. This can make the design more predictable and extend runtime. Typical candidates: 1 Refrigerator and freezer. 1 Selected lights and outlets. 1 Internet and communications.

chunks.sourceTitle: Power You Control: Australian Home Energy Systems Guide
chunks.text: 1 Selected lights and outlets. 1 Internet and communications. 1 Medical and accessibility equipment after specialist review. 1 Security equipment. 1 Water, wastewater or fire-related pumps where technically suitable. 1 One modest heating or cooling zone if output and energy allow. Whole-home backup The system can supply the main board subject to battery and inverter limits. High-power loads may still need automatic shedding or manual discipline. Whole-home connection does not mean unlimited power. Backup design questions 1 What causes transfer and how fast does it occur? 1 Which circuits are backed up? 1 What continuous and surge power is available? 1 Can solar operate and recharge during the outage? 1 Can the system black-start after the battery reaches its minimum? 1 What minimum state of charge is reserved? 1 Does reserve reduce everyday savings?

chunks.sourceTitle: Power You Control: Australian Home Energy Systems Guide
chunks.text: 1 What minimum state of charge is reserved? 1 Does reserve reduce everyday savings? 1 What happens during a cloudy multi-day outage? 1 Can the home reconnect automatically and safely? 1 Will the system work without internet or the provider's cloud? 1 Are smoke alarms, medical equipment and pumps compatible with transfer? 1 How will occupants know they are in backup mode?

chunks.sourceTitle: Power You Control: Australian Home Energy Systems Guide
chunks.text: POWER YOU CONTROL AUSTRALIAN HOME ENERGY SYSTEMS GUIDE Snapshot: 25 August 2026 44 Outage operating plan 1 Confirm the outage is external and keep clear of damaged lines. 2 Check the system status without opening equipment. 3 Turn off discretionary high loads. 4 Protect refrigeration by limiting door opening. 5 Use one heating or cooling zone only if the system supports it. 6 Charge communications and medical devices early. 7 Monitor state of charge and expected weather. 8 Preserve a reserve for overnight or critical equipment. 9 Follow the documented restart process after supply returns. Test backup periodically under the installer's approved procedure. Record whether circuits transfer, solar recharges, alarms work and occupants understand the limits. Generator safety Never connect a generator to household wiring through a power outlet or improvised lead.

chunks.sourceTitle: Power You Control: Australian Home Energy Systems Guide
chunks.text: Record whether circuits transfer, solar recharges, alarms work and occupants understand the limits. Generator safety Never connect a generator to household wiring through a power outlet or improvised lead. A compliant generator connection requires proper changeover or transfer equipment and licensed electrical work. Operate combustion generators outdoors, well away from doors, windows and vents, following carbon-monoxide and fire safety guidance. For off-grid or extended backup, define fuel storage, maintenance, starting reliability, noise, emissions and who can operate it safely. Portable power stations Portable battery systems can power compatible plug-in loads and may help renters. Compare: 1 Usable Wh and continuous or surge W. 1 AC outlet rating and waveform. 1 Solar-input voltage and current limits. 1 Charging time from grid, vehicle or portable solar.

chunks.sourceTitle: Power You Control: Australian Home Energy Systems Guide
chunks.text: 1 Solar-input voltage and current limits. 1 Charging time from grid, vehicle or portable solar. 1 Battery management and tested safety. 1 Ventilation, storage temperature and water protection. 1 Pass-through charging behaviour. 1 Grounding and whether equipment requires special protection. 1 Warranty, repair and end-of-life pathway. Do not use a portable power station to energise fixed household wiring. Do not run leads through wet areas, across escape paths or under doors where damaged. Keep lithium equipment away from exits and combustible storage. Medical and accessibility planning Do not rely on a consumer battery calculation alone for life-support or critical medical equipment. Record manufacturer power requirements, startup behaviour, required runtime, battery internal backup, alarm operation and service-provider instructions.

chunks.sourceTitle: Power You Control: Australian Home Energy Systems Guide
chunks.text: Medical and accessibility planning Do not rely on a consumer battery calculation alone for life-support or critical medical equipment. Record manufacturer power requirements, startup behaviour, required runtime, battery internal backup, alarm operation and service-provider instructions. Register for available life-support protections with the energy retailer and network, and maintain an emergency relocation or alternate-supply plan. Resilience beyond electricity 1 Working smoke alarms and safe lighting.

chunks.text: POWER YOU CONTROL AUSTRALIAN HOME ENERGY SYSTEMS GUIDE Snapshot: 25 August 2026 45 1 Communications, radio and charged power banks. 1 Safe drinking water and non-electric access where needed. 1 Food safety plan. 1 Manual garage or gate release knowledge. 1 Safe indoor temperature plan and a place to relocate. 1 Bushfire, flood, storm and heatwave plans. 1 Printed shutdown instructions and emergency contacts.
